title: Architectural approach for Hacker-Style Encrypted Messaging Interface
context: The requirement demands a high-fidelity 'Cyber-noir' aesthetic involving complex visual effects (Matrix rain, scanlines, glassmorphism) and dynamic state-based animations (decryption, pulsing). The architecture must balance these heavy visual effects with a responsive messaging interface.
decision: Implement a layered rendering architecture: 1) A dedicated HTML5 Canvas layer for the 'Matrix' background to ensure high-performance animation of thousands of characters. 2) A CSS-driven UI layer for the glassmorphic components, utilizing CSS filters and variables for the 'Cyber-noir' theme. 3) A state-driven animation controller to manage the 'Decryption' and 'Pulse' effects independently of the UI logic.
alternativesConsidered: Pure CSS/SVG for Matrix Rain: Rejected due to the high overhead of managing thousands of DOM elements or SVG paths for the falling character effect.
WebGL for background effects: Rejected as it introduces unnecessary complexity and overhead for a 2D canvas-based visual effect.

positive: High visual fidelity and immersive user experience.
Separation of concerns between the visual effects (Canvas) and the UI components (DOM/CSS).
Scalable styling via CSS variables for easy theme adjustments.
negative: Increased client-side resource consumption due to the continuous Canvas animation loop.
Potential performance overhead on low-end mobile devices.
risks: Potential frame drops if the Canvas loop is not optimized.
Accessibility concerns regarding the 'flicker' and 'scanline' effects for sensitive users.
